subject.title: feat(workspace): add tiered bootstrap loading with configurable bootstrapTier

question: Should OpenClaw accept a defaults-wide `agents.defaults.bootstrapTier` config surface after preserving pending `BOOTSTRAP.md`, or should tiered bootstrap policy move to a narrower per-agent/bootstrap-profile design?
rationale: The code blocker is mechanical, but the permanent public config contract affects prompt context, setup behavior, hook extras, and overlapping bootstrap-control proposals in a way automation should not decide alone.

options.title: Accept after safety repair
options.body: Land this direction once pending root `BOOTSTRAP.md` is preserved, docs explain the tiers, and focused resolver/hook/schema tests cover the contract.

options.title: Redesign as bootstrap profiles
options.body: Pause this PR and use the existing per-agent bootstrap profile direction for a narrower, less global policy surface.

options.title: Decline the config knob
options.body: Close the PR and keep users on current controls such as `contextInjection`, bootstrap budgets, and hook configuration.

recommendation.title: Accept after safety repair
recommendation.body: Land this direction once pending root `BOOTSTRAP.md` is preserved, docs explain the tiers, and focused resolver/hook/schema tests cover the contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Prior review context and original subagent bootstrap filtering history make this the clearest owner for the product/API choice.
